passages.provision_quote: On conviction of an offense under this article, the judge shall enter an order that requires the person to return to the foreign nation from which the person entered or attempted to enter the United States or the person's nation of origin.
passages.note: Bill text page prints the operative return-order provision alongside unrelated fentanyl-sentencing, public-benefit document-fraud and e-verify sections.
Bill history page for the same instrument; it names the prime sponsor and the tallies but not Shope's vote.

rows.reasoning: Shope voted Aye on HCR2060 (2024) ("SHOPE Y", Senate Third Reading, "Passed 16-13-1-0-0"), a referral that combines a new state illegal-entry offense and court orders to return with fentanyl sentencing, public-benefit document fraud and e-verify fraud, so under the vote ladder a final-passage vote on it shows direction at most. Its return-order sections reach only people who enter outside a port of entry after the article becomes enforceable, which speaks to removal of recent crossers; the measure nowhere says that settled undocumented immigrants stay, so the second clause of "Focus deportation on recent arrivals while leaving long-settled undocumented immigrants in place" is unstated. No source carries Shope's own words tying his vote to any removal clause, so the evidence establishes the enforcement side only.
